order: Lee's team remained shorthanded, with Celtic winger Yang Hyun-jun out with a hamstring injury and captain Lee Gi-hyuk sidelined with a foot injury.
Lee, who joined the national team a few days after his teammates due to his commitment with his Swiss club Grasshopper, has now scored three goals in the past two matches.

Wang Yudong scored first for China in the 22nd minute after fending off several South Korean set-piece opportunities. As Mao Weijie floated a pass toward the box from the middle of the field, Wang sprinted behind the napping South Korean defense and let the ball bounce off his chest before scoring off his left foot.

"I had not been happy with the way I had been playing, and I am glad I finally scored one," Bae said, after being held off the board in the previous three matches. "This is one of the happiest moments of my life. Now we have one more match to go. Even if I don't get to score one myself, I will try to create space for my teammates to get it done."
South Korea struggled against physical Chinese defense for most of the match and dodged a bullet when defender Kim Ji-soo nearly headed a Chinese cross into his own goal in the 79th minute.
Coach Lee said he was not sure if either player will be available for Saturday's final.

Then in the 82nd minute, Bae netted the go-ahead marker for South Korea, with Eom once again being the setup man. Eom sent a well-placed cross from outside the left edge of the box, and Bae redirected it with his head for the 2-1 lead that South Korea did not relinquish.

Lee Young-jun and Bae Jun-ho scored a goal apiece for the under-23 men's national team in the semifinals at Nagai Stadium in Osaka, some 140 kilometers west of the main host city Nagoya, as South Korea moved within a victory of winning their fourth straight gold medal.
